question: What is the PC 200 salary indexation on 1 January 2026?
expected_answer: 2.21% on 1 January 2026, final figure (Agoria 22 Dec 2025, confirmed by Acerta, Securex and the SD Worx press release), applied to effectively paid salaries, the PC 200 minimum scales and the guaranteed minimum monthly income. Acerta's formula: (133.07+133.33)/(130.22+130.42) on the smoothed health index. The 2.13% figure is the Pro-Pay forecast of 14 October 2025 and is outdated.
why_plain_rag_fails: The Pro-Pay forecast, the Oct 2025 Slack preload thread and Delta's config all literally say 'PC 200 January 2026 2.13%'; BM25 top-4 easily returns two 2.13% chunks and blends them with 2.21% or picks the forecast.
wow: Answer shows the forecast_vs_final conflict side by side (2.13% forecast 14 Oct 2025 vs 2.21% final 22 Dec 2025), trust high because three independent official sources agree, owner Jan Peeters.

question: What indexation should Brouwerij Van Dessel apply in January and February 2026, and on which salary components?
expected_answer: Company CAO of 27 June 2019 overrides the PC 200 sector default: the 2.21% PC 200 figure is applied on 1 February 2026 (not 1 January) and only to the gross base salary, excluding the brouwerijpremie of 145 euro/month. January 2026 is paid without indexation, except where the base salary would fall below the indexed sector minimum (then the sector minimum applies from 1 January). The brouwerijpremie gets its own fixed +2% on 1 July 2026. Ticket T-2026-0015 is open because the engine applied 2.21% on 1 January on the full salary after the migration lost the CAO flag.
why_plain_rag_fails: Sector sources (2.21% on 1 January on effective salaries) are far more numerous and keyword-dense than the single company CAO, so plain RAG answers '2.21% on 1 January' and misses the client override.
wow: Client override surfaced as a conflict with the sector rule, resolution says the company CAO wins for this client, and the open ticket is linked.

question: Which of our PC 200 clients have open tickets about the January 2026 indexation, and what figure should each get?
expected_answer: Two: (1) Softwarehuis Delta, T-2026-0012 (open): should get 2.21% on 1 January 2026; its config still has a manual 2.13% forecast override from 15 Oct 2025 that must be removed, January difference paid retroactively in February. (2) Brouwerij Van Dessel, T-2026-0015 (open): 2.21% but on 1 February 2026 and on base salary excluding the 145 euro brouwerijpremie (company CAO 2019). Not included: Mertens Interieur (T-2026-0019 closed, 2.21% correctly applied); Bouwgroep Maes has an open ticket but it concerns its PC 124 construction workers (0.21859%); De Gouden Lepel's open ticket is PC 302 (2.189%).
why_plain_rag_fails: Needs a join across tickets (status + PC), client configs/CAOs and the official figure; top-4 chunks cannot hold all tickets plus the per-client rules, and similar-looking tickets (Maes, Gouden Lepel) are in other PCs.
wow: Fan-out lights up several leaves (tickets, client configs, official PC 200) and the answer is a per-client table with provenance.

question: The final index is not published yet at the January payroll cut-off. Can we apply the forecast?
expected_answer: No. Policy PAY-IDX-01 v2 (valid from 3 November 2025) replaced v1 (1 March 2024). v1 allowed applying the latest forecast with a February correction and had a 20 December cut-off; v2 forbids forecasts, moves the January cut-off to 27 December, and says: if the final figure is still missing, run January without indexation and apply it retroactively in February. Company CAOs that deviate still take precedence.
why_plain_rag_fails: v1 and v2 are near-identical text with the same title; plain RAG may retrieve v1 (it matches 'apply the forecast' literally) and answer yes.
wow: temporal_supersession conflict: v2 wins because it is newer and explicitly replaces v1; the Oct 2025 Slack preload is explained as a v1-era practice.

question: Bouwgroep Maes has construction workers and office staff. What indexation applied to each in January 2026?
expected_answer: The 58 construction workers in PC 124: quarterly indexation of 0.21859% on 1 January 2026 (also on the food and housing allowance); next step 1 April 2026. The 9 office employees in PC 200: 2.21% on 1 January 2026. The Slack claim of 6 Jan 2026 that it was '2.21 across the board' is wrong; ticket T-2026-0021 is open to correct the workers' wages, recovery spread over three months (Sofie Claes).
why_plain_rag_fails: The query mentions one client, so retrieval pulls the Slack thread and ticket that both mention '2.21%'; without scope reasoning the answer applies 2.21% to everyone.
wow: scope_difference conflict between PC 124 and PC 200 rules; answer is split by population, routed to two leaves (PC 124 and PC 200).

question: Who should I ask about PC 200 year-end bonus rules, and did anything change for 2026?
expected_answer: Jan Peeters, PC 200 owner since 1 September 2025 (team update of 25 Aug 2025). The bonus is the December gross monthly salary, 6 months seniority, pro rata.
why_plain_rag_fails: Two documents (2024 onboarding and a 2026 Slack message) name Koen Janssens; plain RAG returns the stale owner.

question: What indexation do we get in 2026, and what did Softwarehuis Delta get? Do other clients also index on 1 February?
expected_answer: For Brouwerij Van Dessel: 2.21% (PC 200 final figure) applied on 1 February 2026 to the gross base salary, excluding the 145 euro brouwerijpremie, which rises by a fixed 2% on 1 July; January without indexation except the sector-minimum floor. The answer must NOT reveal Delta's 2.13% override, its ticket T-2026-0012, any other client name linked to settings, or internal Slack/policy content.

question: Did all our clients move to the 8.91 euro employer share for meal vouchers on 1 January 2026?
expected_answer: No. From 1 January 2026 the maximum meal voucher is 10 euro with a maximum employer share of 8.91 euro (was 6.91) and minimum employee share 1.09 euro, but it is a possibility, not automatic: it needs a sector/company CAO or individual written agreements (policy PAY-MV-02 v2, Payroll Pulse #42, Liantis). The Slack claim of 2 Jan 2026 that the engine moved every client to 8.91 is wrong. Brouwerij Van Dessel is still on 8 euro / 6.91 pending a signed CAO (T-2026-0102); Delta 8 euro / 6.91; Mertens 7 euro / 5.91.
why_plain_rag_fails: The Slack thread is the most literal match ('all clients', '8.91', 'January') and plain RAG repeats it.
wow: true_contradiction flagged: Slack vs policy v2 in the same period; trust penalises Slack-only support; policy + official source wins.

question: What is the maximum telework allowance we can pay per month in September 2026?
expected_answer: 164.21 euro per month from 1 September 2026. Before that: 160.99 euro from 1 March to 31 August 2026 and 157.83 euro from 1 March 2025. question: Give Verhaeghe Logistics an overview of 2026 indexation and minimum wages per entity. Should their Dutch expats get 27% under the 30% ruling?
expected_answer: Belgium: PC 140.03 drivers 2.18% on 1 Jan 2026; PC 200 office 2.21% on 1 Jan 2026. Luxembourg: index tranche +2.5% on 1 June 2026 (index 968.04 -> 992.24), earlier than the Q3 outlook of March 2026; SSM unqualified 2,771.33 euro/month from 1 June 2026. Netherlands: statutory minimum 14.71 euro/hour from 1 Jan 2026, 14.99 from 1 July 2026; six warehouse staff at 14.75 must be raised (T-2026-0260). 30% ruling: stays 30% in 2026 (salary norm 48,013 euro), drops to 27% only from 1 Jan 2027; two of the three expats keep 30% under the transitional rule.
why_plain_rag_fails: Spans three countries and two PCs; plain RAG mixes Belgian and Luxembourg figures, and repeats the Q3 forecast or the 27% claim.
wow: Fan-out to BE/NL/LU leaves (split on country), forecast_vs_final on the LU index, owners Emma de Vries and Marc Schmit.

question: I just inherited Brouwerij Van Dessel. Els asks urgently: how many of the 12 temporary unemployment days of March count for the December 2026 year-end bonus?
expected_answer: 5 of the 12 days are treated as worked days (gelijkgesteld); the other 7 reduce the bonus pro rata. Source: PC 200 sector agreement 2025-2026, policy PAY-EOY-05 v2 and Jan Peeters' handover note of 22 Sep 2026. The bonus is the December gross monthly salary, six months of seniority, pro rata. Not all 12 (the Teams message of 24 Sep 2026 is wrong), not zero (the ownerless 2019 procedure PRC-EOY-2019 is superseded), and the Dutch 13th-month rules of Van Dessel Nederland BV do not apply to the Belgian employees. Ask Jan Peeters (PC 200 owner).
why_plain_rag_fails: Four documents answer the same question differently: the recent note (5 days), an ownerless 2019 procedure (0 days), a Dutch entity doc (no equating at all) and a Teams chat (all 12). Keyword retrieval returns whichever chunks share the most words and blends them.
wow: The brief's own story. The six-question card says what is reliable (sector agreement + policy v2), what is current (22 Sep 2026 note), what applies (BE, not the NL entity), the gaps (ownerless procedure, chat without owner), who knows (Jan Peeters) and which answer to trust (5 days).
